To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hypothalamic- pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis plays a fundamental role in obesity and energy balance in the genetically obese Zucker rat.
HYPX in obese Zucker rats significantly reduced food intake, body weight, and energy balance and increased energy expenditure, the thermic response of food, and BAT activity.

hypophysectomy (removal of the anterior pituitary) of obese Zucker rats reduces body fat, stimulates energy expenditure, increases the thermic response of brown fat, and reduces the thermic response and activity of brown fat in lean rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of brown adipose tissue and its thermogenic capacity in the regulation of energy balance in the obese Zucker rat.
the role of brown adipose tissue and energy balance in the pathogenesis of obesity and its treatment.

the role of the hypothalamus in regulating energy balance, and in particular with the role of corticotrophin-releasing hormone (CRH) in the control of food intake, energy expenditure, and body composition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HYPX in genetically obese rats (fa/fa) significantly reduced body weight, food intake, energy gain, and the thermic response of food.
HYPX in genetically obese rats significantly reduced bodyweight and energy gains and increased energy expenditure and the thermic response of food, but only partially restored BAT activity.
HYPX in obese Zucker rats significantly reduced energy balance and increased BAT activity and thermogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HYPX in the genetically obese Zucker rat results in a significant reduction of body weight gain, energy intake, and energy expenditure and an increase in the acute thermic effect of food and BAT mitochondrial activity.
the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis is involved in the regulation of energy balance, and that it may be the primary cause of obesity in the Zucker rat.
the hypothalamo-pituitary axis is involved in the development and regulation of obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HYPX in obese (fa/fa), but not lean (+/?) rats, resulted in marked reductions in body weight gain, food intake, and energy balance.
the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis is involved in obesity.
the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis may play an important role in the development of obesity in Zucker rats.
